messages:
alex: Quick sync — we're rolling a new runtime metrics dashboard next week (latency-by-model, kv_cache_hit_rate, queue_depth, gpu_util_p95). Need to lock alerting thresholds and oncall routing before deployment. @sre / @eng-runtime please chime in.

maria: thanks Alex. can we get the expected baseline for kv_cache_hit_rate and queue_depth per-model? will affect sane thresholds.

kevin: from SRE side: recommend two-alert strategy: 1) short-term burn alert (5m) for sudden spike in SLO error or queue_depth, 2) sustained degradation (1h) for paging. short term should notify channel only, sustained should page.

liam: +1 on two-tier. also want to attach runbook link in alert. For paging rules: SEV1 -> platform-oncall, SEV2 -> component-owner -> platform-oncall fallback. SEV3 -> slack channel only.

alex: noted. proposed numeric thresholds to discuss: 
- queue_depth > 250 for 5m -> channel alert
- queue_depth > 200 for 1h -> page SEV2
- gpu_util_p95 > 96% for 5m -> channel
- gpu_util_p95 > 98% for 15m -> page SEV1
- kv_cache_hit_rate < 60% for 10m -> page SEV2

maria: those look reasonable as starting points. one caveat: model X usually spikes queue_depth to ~220 for short bursts during batch jobs at 03:00 UTC. recommend we scope alerts to production traffic only (route labels: traffic_type!=batch).

kevin: good call. add label match to all rules: `traffic_type="interactive"` and ignore metric series where `job=offline-maint`. also suggest using burn-rate for SLOs instead of raw error rate. e.g. burn > 3x for 5m -> channel, burn > 6x for 1h -> page.

sanjay: observability notes: we'll add panels for p95/p99, moving windows, and show historical baselines. I'll add an example alert proto in PagerDuty integration YAML. preview: 
````yaml
- name: runtime-queue-depth-sev2
  expr: sum(rate(queue_depth{traffic_type="interactive"}[5m])) by (model) > 200
  for: 1h
  labels:
    severity: "sev2"
  annotations:
    summary: "Runtime queue depth high for {{ $labels.model }}"
    runbook: "https://redwood.internal/runbooks/runtime-queue"
````

liam: confirm PD routing: severity label -> map to PD escalation policy: sev1->policy/platform-sev1, sev2->policy/component-owner, fallback->policy/platform-escalation. Can ops-bot create the PD policies if missing?

ops-bot: created ticket OPS-4921 to provision PD policies and webhook integration. ETA 2 business days. :robot_face:

alex: next steps: (1) eng-runtime to add traffic_type label + verify model X exception, (2) observability to add panels + draft alert rules (use burn-rate expressions), (3) SRE to confirm PD policies & escalation mapping, (4) platform to stage dashboard in staging and run a 24h smoke. can everyone ack?

maria: ack — I'll add label and push a PR for the metric export by EOD tomorrow.

kevin: ack from SRE. will review alert rules and add suppression for deploy windows.

sanjay: ack, I'll push dashboard PR and attach example alerts.

liam: ack, will validate PD mapping once OPS-4921 completes.

alex: thanks all. I'll schedule a 30m sync Wed to finalize thresholds and signoff. :calendar:
